subject: Media Literacy
title: The Myth of Perfect Objectivity
description: A fast breakdown of The Myth of Perfect Objectivity for builders.

hook.text: Journalists pledge objectivity. But choosing which story to cover at all is already a subjective decision.

buildup.text: Objectivity means reporting facts without personal opinion. It's been journalism's gold standard for a century.

discovery.text: But even 'objective' reporting requires choices — what to include, who to quote, how to frame the story.

twist.text: The objectivity standard can itself be biased — treating 'both sides' equally even when evidence favors one.

climax.text: Demanding perfect objectivity is unrealistic. Demanding transparency about perspective is achievable and more useful.

punchline.text: Objectivity is a goal, not a state. Transparency is the honest alternative.

quiz.question: Why is perfect objectivity in journalism considered a myth?
options: Every editorial choice involves subjective judgment about what to include and how
